result.description: Work management platform for teams to plan, track and automate tasks, projects, and portfolios.
result.auth_detail: OAuth2 auth-code (app registered in developer console; also OIDC) for multi-user apps; Personal Access Token (Bearer header) that any user self-creates; Service Accounts (Enterprise tier, super admin only).
result.access_detail: Free dev console signup; each user can mint a PAT free, and the Free tier has API access (150 req/min). OAuth app can be created without review and used in own org; to let users in any other workspace connect via OAuth, app must be submitted for review and published. Per-user PATs avoid that gate. Service Accounts need Enterprise.
result.api_notes: REST API covers tasks, projects, sections, portfolios, goals, users, workspaces, teams, custom fields, attachments, webhooks, events, batch, search, etc. Rate limit 150/min Free, 1500/min Paid. OpenAPI spec and SDKs available.
result.blocker: Public multi-tenant OAuth distribution (any workspace) requires Asana app review/publish; PAT path works self-serve with no review. Service Accounts Enterprise-only.

evidence.quote: A personal access token (PAT) is the quickest and simplest way to authenticate in the API.
Service Accounts are an Enterprise tier feature and can only be created by Asana super admins
The endpoint for token exchange is POST https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_token
Make your app available to users in any Asana workspace, beyond your own organization or development environment
If you're building an internal tool or testing your integration, you can create and use an OAuth app without submitting it for review.
Limits are based on minute-long windows and differ depending on whether the domain is free or paid (see pricing for available tiers).
generating a PAT allows you to access (i.e., make requests to) the Asana REST API upon successful authentication.
The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.
